title: Universal Anti-CD70 CAR-T (CHT101) Cell Therapy for Relapsed Refractory Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
off: A Clinical Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Universal Anti-CD70 CAR-T (CHT101) for the Treatment of Relapsed and Refractory Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
sponsor: The Affiliated Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital of Nanjing University Medical School

officials.a: The Affiliated Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital of Nanjing University Medical School

summary: This investigator-initiated trial aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of universal anti-CD70 CAR-T (CHT101) in patients with relapsed refractory systemic lupus erythematosus.
desc: This study is a non-randomized, open-label, single-arm clinical trial designed to assess the efficacy and safety of universal anti-CD70 CAR-T (CHT101) in patients with relapsed refractory systemic lupus erythematosus.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Meet the 2019 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
2. SLEDAI-2000 score \>6.
3. Have at least one BILAG-2004 Grade A or two Grade B organ domain scores, or both.
4. Failure to respond to conventional therapy or disease relapse after remission. Conventional therapy: Glucocorticoids (≥1 mg/kg/day) combined with cyclophosphamide and ≥1 of the following immunosuppressants for \>6 months: antimalarials, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, methotrexate, leflunomide, tacrolimus, cyclosporine A, and/or biologics (e.g., rituximab, belimumab, telitacicept).
5. Aged 18-65 years; both genders eligible.
6. Adequate organ function:Bone marrow function: White blood cell count ≥3×10⁹/L. Absolute neutrophil count ≥1×10⁹/L (without colony-stimulating factor therapy within 2 weeks prior to testing). Hemoglobin ≥60 g/L; Liver function: Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤3×upper limit of normal (ULN). Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤3×ULN. Total bilirubin (TBIL) ≤1.5×ULN (except Gilbert's syndrome, TBIL ≤3.0×ULN); Renal function: Creatinine clearance (CrCl) ≥60 mL/min (calculated by Cockcroft-Gault formula); Coagulation: International normalized ratio (INR) ≤1.5×ULN. Prothrombin time (PT) ≤1.5×ULN; Cardiac function: Hemodynamic stability with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥55%.
7. Agrees to use double barrier methods, condoms, oral or injectable contraceptives, or intrauterine devices during the study period and for one year after taking the study medication. Females of childbearing potential must have a negative serum HCG test within 7 days prior to enrollment and must not be lactating.
8. Voluntarily participate in the study, provide written informed consent, and demonstrate good compliance with follow-up.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Presence of neuropsychiatric lupus (NPSLE).
2. History of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) or thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA).
3. History of severe drug allergies or hypersensitivity.
4. Active or suspected uncontrolled infections requiring treatment (including fungal, bacterial, viral, or other pathogens).
5. Central nervous system disorders caused by autoimmune diseases (ADs) or non-ADs.
6. Severe cardiac diseases.
7. Congenital immunoglobulin deficiency.
8. History of malignancy (except non-melanoma skin cancer, in situ cervical/bladder/breast/thyroid carcinoma with disease-free survival \>5 years).
9. End-stage renal failure.
10. Participants meeting any of the following: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive or hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb)-positive with detectable HBV DNA; Hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody-positive with detectable HCV RNA; HIV antibody-positive; Syphilis-positive (RPR and TPHA positive, or TPHA positive with RPR reconfirmed positive after 4 weeks).
11. Psychiatric disorders or severe cognitive impairment.
12. Participation in other clinical trials within 3 months prior to enrollment.
13. Pregnant women or those planning pregnancy.
14. Other conditions deemed by the investigator to preclude study participation.

primary.tf: SRI-4 response assessed at Month 3 after CHT101 infusion.
safety evaluation Within 12 months after CHT101 infusion.

x.titre: CAR-T universel anti-CD70 (CHT101) dans le lupus systémique réfractaire ou en rechute
x.question: Le CAR-T universel anti-CD70 CHT101 est-il sûr et efficace dans le lupus systémique réfractaire ou en rechute ?
x.contexte:
Une partie des patients lupiques reste en échec malgré des doses élevées de corticoïdes, le cyclophosphamide, les immunosuppresseurs et les biothérapies (rituximab, bélimumab, télitacicept). Les CAR-T anti-CD19 autologues ont obtenu des rémissions dans des séries de lupus réfractaire.

CD70 est exprimé sur des lymphocytes T et B activés, ce qui motive une approche ciblant les cellules immunitaires activées plutôt que l'ensemble des lymphocytes B. Le CHT101 est un CAR-T universel (allogénique) dirigé contre CD70.

Cette étude de phase 1 à promotion académique, ouverte et monobras, est menée à l'hôpital Drum Tower de Nanjing. Elle prévoit environ 15 patients de 18 à 65 ans, avec un lupus actif (SLEDAI-2K > 6, BILAG A ou deux B) en échec du traitement conventionnel ou en rechute. Les critères principaux sont la réponse SRI-4 au mois 3 et la tolérance à 12 mois.
x.interet: L'étude apportera des premiers résultats de tolérance et d'efficacité d'un CAR-T allogénique ciblant une nouvelle protéine dans le lupus. Elle reste exploratoire, sans comparateur.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 65 ans atteints de lupus systémique actif, réfractaire ou en rechute.
inclusion: SLEDAI-2K > 6, au moins un BILAG A ou deux BILAG B
Échec du traitement conventionnel (corticoïdes ≥ 1 mg/kg/jour, cyclophosphamide, immunosuppresseurs ou biothérapie) ou rechute après rémission
Contraception pendant 1 an après le traitement
exclusion: Antécédent de purpura thrombotique thrombocytopénique ou de microangiopathie thrombotique
Infection active ou suspectée non contrôlée
Atteinte du système nerveux central d'origine auto-immune

bras.traitement: Perfusion de CHT101 ; dose et schéma de lymphodéplétion non précisés

x.critere: Réponse SRI-4 au mois 3 après la perfusion et tolérance dans les 12 mois
